tagline: The shopping-and-eating capital of the deep south — Kim Yong market, Khlong Hae floating market, the park cable car, and fried chicken with dim sum
introHtml:
Hat Yai is the commercial heart of Songkhla province and the trade, food, and travel hub of the lower south. It sits close to the Malaysian border, so Malaysian and Singaporean visitors cross over to shop and eat in big numbers — which keeps the city buzzing day and night.

The pull of Hat Yai is its markets — Kim Yong and Santisuk sell imported snacks and goods, Khlong Hae is a floating market where vendors paddle boats selling southern Thai food, and Greenway–ASEAN is the night-market scene. For temple visits and views there's Hat Yai Municipal Park, where you ride a cable car up to pay respects at the giant Phra Buddha Mongkol Maharaj, the Brahma shrine, and a large Guanyin statue on the hill. Food is the real star here — Hat Yai fried chicken, morning dim sum, chicken rice, and a comfortable blend of Chinese and southern cooking. Come to Hat Yai to eat, shop, and use it as a base for exploring Songkhla and the lower south.
bestTime: Good year-round (lots of indoor spots and markets) · December–February has the best weather, while November–December is the rainy stretch for the Gulf side of the south

highlights.name: Kim Yong and Santisuk markets
highlights.blurb: Markets in central Hat Yai selling imported snacks and goods — sweets, chocolate, nuts, dried squid, and souvenirs. You can browse all day; it's one of the city's defining sights.

highlights.name: Khlong Hae Floating Market
highlights.blurb: An old floating market where vendors paddle boats selling southern Thai food along the canal. Open Friday–Sunday, it's a nice spot to graze and eat by the water.

highlights.name: Hat Yai Municipal Park and cable car
highlights.blurb: A hilltop park in the city where you ride the cable car up to pay respects at Phra Buddha Mongkol Maharaj, the Brahma shrine, and a large Guanyin statue, with views over Hat Yai in every direction.

highlights.name: Greenway–ASEAN night market
highlights.blurb: The night market around Lee Gardens and Greenway brings together street food, snacks, and shopping, open late — it's the city's after-dark eating and drinking quarter.

highlights.name: Hat Yai fried chicken and dim sum
highlights.blurb: Hat Yai fried chicken with its crisp skin and crispy fried shallots, paired with morning dim sum, is the signature local eat everyone has to try. You can find it all over town from morning to late night.

highlights.name: A base for Songkhla and the lower south
highlights.blurb: Hat Yai is a handy stopover and launch point for old-town Songkhla, Samila Beach, Ton Nga Chang waterfall, and crossing into Malaysia — easy by train, coach, or plane.

foodScene.name: Hat Yai fried chicken
foodScene.note: Fried chicken with crisp skin scattered with fried shallots, eaten with sticky rice or steamed rice and dipping sauce. It's the city's number-one famous dish, with several well-known shops.

foodScene.name: Morning dim sum
foodScene.note: Dim sum shops open at the crack of dawn — har gow, shumai, steamed buns, and Chinese tea. It's a southern-Chinese breakfast culture that's part of Hat Yai.

foodScene.name: Chicken rice and red pork rice
foodScene.note: Hat Yai chicken rice with fragrant oiled rice and tender chicken, plus red pork and crispy pork rice, are popular lunches at the city's old shops.

foodScene.name: Bold southern Thai food
foodScene.note: Gaeng tai pla, gaeng leuang, khua kling, and khao yam are everywhere in town — punchy, spicy and salty, eaten with hot steamed rice and fresh raw vegetables on the side.

foodScene.name: Chinese food and banquet tables
foodScene.note: With the city's Chinese roots, Hat Yai has plenty of Chinese restaurants, dim sum, and banquet spreads — roast duck, crispy pork, and southern-Chinese-style seafood dishes.

foodScene.name: Street food and night markets
foodScene.note: The Greenway, Lee Gardens, and ASEAN night-market areas gather snacks, grills, fried bites, and sweets to graze on after dark.

foodScene.name: Cafes and coffee
foodScene.note: The city has plenty of fresh-coffee cafes and new brunch spots, both downtown and near the university — good for working or taking a break from shopping.

foodScene.name: Hat Yai souvenirs
foodScene.note: Dried squid, grilled squid, mooncake-style pastries, cashews, and imported goods from Kim Yong market are souvenirs almost everyone takes home.

attractions.name: Hat Yai Municipal Park and cable car
attractions.blurb: A hilltop park in the city; ride the cable car up to pay respects at Phra Buddha Mongkol Maharaj, the Brahma shrine, and a large Guanyin statue, and take in views across the city.

attractions.name: Kim Yong Market
attractions.blurb: A central market for imported snacks and goods — sweets, chocolate, dried squid, souvenirs — to browse all day. It's the shopping anchor of Hat Yai.

attractions.name: Khlong Hae Floating Market
attractions.blurb: An old floating market where vendors paddle boats selling southern Thai food along the canal. Open Friday–Sunday, it's a place to graze on local eats and sit by the water.

attractions.name: Wat Hat Yai Nai (Reclining Buddha)
attractions.blurb: A city temple with one of the longest reclining Buddha statues in the south — a spot to pay respects and admire the Buddhist art close to downtown.

attractions.name: Ton Nga Chang Waterfall
attractions.blurb: A multi-tier waterfall in the Khao Kaeo range forest near Hat Yai, with clear cool water, short hikes, and swimming — a favorite nature getaway for locals.

attractions.name: ASEAN Night Bazaar and Greenway
attractions.blurb: A night market around Lee Gardens gathering street food, shopping, and snacks, open late — the after-dark strip for eating and drinking.

attractions.name: Museums and city photo spots
attractions.blurb: Hat Yai has a 3D art museum, street art, and photo corners around town to wander between meals and shopping trips.

attractions.name: Old-town Songkhla and Samila (nearby)
attractions.blurb: About a 30-minute drive from Hat Yai to old-town Songkhla's Sino-Portuguese buildings and Samila Beach with its golden mermaid — an easy half-day trip to add on.

itineraryIdeas: Hat Yai 2D1N — Kim Yong market, the cable car, and fried chicken with dim sum
Hat Yai for foodies — morning dim sum, chicken rice, and the night market
Hat Yai for shopping and souvenirs — Kim Yong, Santisuk, and the ASEAN night market
Hat Yai for temples and views — the park, the cable car, and the Reclining Buddha temple
Hat Yai to Songkhla — the Sino old town and Samila Beach
Hat Yai to Ton Nga Chang — a half-day waterfall trip
